description: Na₃CaTi₃Fe₅O₁₆ crystallizes in the monoclinic Pm space group. There are three inequivalent Na sites. In the first Na site, Na is bonded to six O atoms to form distorted NaO₆ octahedra that share corners with two equivalent NaO₆ octahedra,  a cornercorner with one FeO₅ square pyramid,  an edgeedge with one FeO₆ octahedra, and edges with two equivalent CaO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles are 15°. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.14-2.51 Å. In the second Na site, Na is bonded to six O atoms to form distorted NaO₆ octahedra that share corners with two equivalent NaO₆ octahedra,  an edgeedge with one FeO₆ octahedra, edges with two equivalent NaO₆ octahedra,  an edgeedge with one FeO₅ square pyramid, and edges with two equivalent FeO₅ trigonal bipyramids. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles are 11°. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.14-2.59 Å. In the third Na site, Na is bonded to six O atoms to form NaO₆ octahedra that share corners with two equivalent NaO₆ octahedra, corners with two equivalent CaO₆ octahedra, edges with two equivalent NaO₆ octahedra, edges with two equivalent FeO₆ octahedra, edges with two equivalent FeO₅ square pyramids, and  an edgeedge with one FeO₅ trigonal bipyramid. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 2-25°. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.13-2.38 Å. Ca is bonded to six O atoms to form CaO₆ octahedra that share corners with two equivalent NaO₆ octahedra, corners with two equivalent CaO₆ octahedra, corners with two equivalent FeO₅ square pyramids,  a cornercorner with one FeO₅ trigonal bipyramid, edges with two equivalent NaO₆ octahedra, and edges with two equivalent FeO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 20-25°. There are a spread of Ca-O bond distances ranging from 2.16-2.37 Å. There are three inequivalent Ti sites. In the first Ti site, Ti is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to six O atoms. There are a spread of Ti-O bond distances ranging from 1.65-2.51 Å. In the second Ti site, Ti is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to six O atoms. There are a spread of Ti-O bond distances ranging from 1.65-2.61 Å. In the third Ti site, Ti is bonded in a 5-coordinate geometry to five O atoms. There are a spread of Ti-O bond distances ranging from 1.72-2.23 Å. There are five inequivalent Fe sites. In the first Fe site, Fe is bonded to five O atoms to form distorted FeO₅ square pyramids that share  a cornercorner with one NaO₆ octahedra,  a cornercorner with one FeO₆ octahedra, corners with two equivalent CaO₆ octahedra, corners with two equivalent FeO₅ square pyramids, and edges with three NaO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 7-85°. There are a spread of Fe-O bond distances ranging from 1.90-2.18 Å. In the second Fe site, Fe is bonded to six O atoms to form FeO₆ octahedra that share corners with two equivalent FeO₆ octahedra,  a cornercorner with one FeO₅ square pyramid, edges with two equivalent CaO₆ octahedra, edges with four NaO₆ octahedra, and edges with two equivalent FeO₅ trigonal bipyramids. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles are 21°. There are a spread of Fe-O bond distances ranging from 1.90-2.31 Å. In the third Fe site, Fe is bonded to five O atoms to form distorted FeO₅ trigonal bipyramids that share  a cornercorner with one CaO₆ octahedra, corners with two equivalent FeO₅ trigonal bipyramids, edges with two equivalent FeO₆ octahedra, and edges with three NaO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles are 69°. There are a spread of Fe-O bond distances ranging from 1.93-2.21 Å. In the fourth Fe site, Fe is bonded in a 5-coordinate geometry to five O atoms. There are a spread of Fe-O bond distances ranging from 1.84-2.32 Å. In the fifth Fe site, Fe is bonded in a 5-coordinate geometry to five O atoms. There are a spread of Fe-O bond distances ranging from 1.82-2.22 Å. There are sixteen inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded to three Na, one Ti, and two Fe atoms to form distorted ONa₃TiFe₂ octahedra that share corners with two equivalent ONa₃TiFe₂ octahedra, edges with four ONaTiFe₃ square pyramids, and edges with six ONaTiFe₃ trigonal bipyramids. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles are 2°. In the second O site, O is bonded in a linear geometry to one Na and one Ti atom. In the third O site, O is bonded to one Na, one Ti, and three Fe atoms to form distorted ONaTiFe₃ trigonal bipyramids that share corners with three ONaTiFe₃ square pyramids, corners with four ONaTiFe₃ trigonal bipyramids,  an edgeedge with one ONa₃TiFe₂ octahedra, and edges with two equivalent ONa₃Fe₂ trigonal bipyramids. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a linear geometry to one Na and one Ti atom. In the fifth O site, O is bonded to one Na, one Ti, and three Fe atoms to form distorted ONaTiFe₃ square pyramids that share corners with two equivalent ONaTiFe₃ square pyramids, corners with three ONaTiFe₃ trigonal bipyramids,  an edgeedge with one ONa₃TiFe₂ octahedra, edges with two equivalent ONa₂CaTiFe square pyramids, and edges with two equivalent ONaCaFe₃ trigonal bipyramids. In the sixth O site, O is bonded to one Na, one Ti, and three Fe atoms to form distorted ONaTiFe₃ square pyramids that share corners with two equivalent ONaTiFe₃ square pyramids, corners with three ONaTiFe₃ trigonal bipyramids,  an edgeedge with one ONa₃TiFe₂ octahedra, edges with two equivalent ONaCaFe₃ square pyramids, and edges with two equivalent ONa₃Fe₂ trigonal bipyramids. In the seventh O site, O is bonded in a 5-coordinate geometry to one Na, two equivalent Ca, one Ti, and one Fe atom. In the eighth O site, O is bonded to one Na, three Ti, and one Fe atom to form distorted ONaTi₃Fe trigonal bipyramids that share corners with five ONaTiFe₃ square pyramids, corners with two equivalent ONaTi₃Fe trigonal bipyramids,  an edgeedge with one ONa₃TiFe₂ octahedra, and edges with two equivalent ONa₂CaTiFe square pyramids. In the ninth O site, O is bonded to two equivalent Na, one Ca, one Ti, and one Fe atom to form distorted ONa₂CaTiFe square pyramids that share corners with three ONa₂CaTiFe square pyramids, edges with two equivalent ONaTiFe₃ square pyramids, and edges with three ONaTi₃Fe trigonal bipyramids. In the tenth O site, O is bonded to one Na, one Ca, and three Fe atoms to form ONaCaFe₃ trigonal bipyramids that share corners with two equivalent ONaCaFe₃ square pyramids, corners with five ONaTiFe₃ trigonal bipyramids, edges with two equivalent ONa₃TiFe₂ octahedra, and edges with three ONaTiFe₃ square pyramids. In the eleventh O site, O is bonded to three Na and two Fe atoms to form ONa₃Fe₂ trigonal bipyramids that share corners with three ONaCaFe₃ trigonal bipyramids, edges with two equivalent ONa₃TiFe₂ octahedra, edges with three ONaCaFe₃ square pyramids, and edges with two equivalent ONaTiFe₃ trigonal bipyramids. In the twelfth O site, O is bonded in a distorted see-saw-like geometry to one Na and three Ti atoms. In the thirteenth O site, O is bonded in a linear geometry to one Ti and one Fe atom. In the fourteenth O site, O is bonded to one Na, one Ca, and three Fe atoms to form ONaCaFe₃ square pyramids that share corners with three ONa₂CaTiFe square pyramids, corners with four ONaTi₃Fe trigonal bipyramids, edges with two equivalent ONa₃TiFe₂ octahedra, edges with two equivalent ONaTiFe₃ square pyramids, and  an edgeedge with one ONa₃Fe₂ trigonal bipyramid. In the fifteenth O site, O is bonded in a distorted see-saw-like geometry to one Ca, two equivalent Ti, and one Fe atom. In the sixteenth O site, O is bonded in a linear geometry to two Fe atoms.
